method.identity_check: Publisher-controlled landing page, title, date, artifact, and where applicable machine endpoint were inspected.
method.fidelity_check: The exact table, chapter, note, or workbook row used by each finding was read in context; units, scope, status, and qualifiers were retained.
method.second_check: Load-bearing numbers were checked against a second publisher-controlled representation, an independent official source, or the downloaded source table itself. Same-artifact checks are explicitly labeled.
method.rejection_rule: A value is excluded when its scenario/year mapping, denominator, or accounting boundary cannot be verified. No interpolation is performed between sparse milestones.

sources.publisher: Our World in Data; underlying electricity-demand source Ember
sources.title: Electricity demand
locators: OWID About this data and Sources and processing
Ember Data Methodology v1.5, Definitions and Electricity Generation and Net Imports
sources.verified_scope: World historical electricity demand from 2000-2025 in the retained OWID file.
critical_notes: Ember defines electricity demand as gross electricity generation plus net imports.
This system-demand boundary is not IEA final electricity consumption and produces a larger total.
World and latest-year figures can include estimates; the 2025 value is not treated as final.
sources.second_check: The OWID data page's source attribution, units, update date, and World records were checked against Ember's official methodology definition and the retained raw CSV.

sources.title: Monthly Energy Review, Table 7.6: Electricity End Use
locators: Table 7.6 CSV series ESRCPUS, ESCCPUS, ESICPUS, ESACPUS, ESTCPUS, ELDUPUS, ELTCPUS, and ESVHPUS
Monthly Energy Review section 7 PDF, Table 7.6 notes
sources.verified_scope: U.S. electricity sales by sector, direct use, total use, and experimental on-road light-duty EV electricity use.
critical_notes: EV use is independently estimated but already included in electricity sales and total use; it must not be added to either total.
The EV method changes beginning in 2023, so the 2018-2022 and 2023-forward segments are not strictly comparable.
The EV series excludes gasoline used by plug-in hybrids and covers on-road light-duty vehicle electricity.
sources.second_check: CSV values were checked against the publisher's table definitions and notes in https://www.eia.gov/totalenergy/data/monthly/pdf/sec7.pdf.

sources.title: Annual Energy Outlook 2026 Reference and Side-Case Tables
locators: yearbyyear.xlsx Tables 4-8, 19, and 20 for baseline and ten side cases
AEO2026 narrative: Consumption and Electricity chapters
sources.verified_scope: Annual U.S. conditional scenario output for 2025-2050: sales, use, generation, sector end uses, data-center servers, EV charging by location, industrial components, and macro drivers.
critical_notes: AEO cases are alternative conditional futures, not probability-weighted forecasts or predictions.
Residential and commercial EV charging is assigned by charging location; transportation-sector sales therefore do not represent all on-road EV charging.
The commercial Data Center Servers row is server electricity, not whole-facility data-center electricity.
Generation, net generation to grid, sales, direct use, and total use have different accounting boundaries.
sources.second_check: Every normalized value is read from the full official case workbook; key endpoint values and case descriptions were cross-checked against EIA narrative text and workbook footnotes.

sources.title: Electricity 2026: Demand
locators: Global demand growth by sector and region
sources.verified_scope: World electricity consumption estimate for 2025, forecast through 2030, and sector/region contributions to growth.
critical_notes: Forecast horizon ends in 2030.
Reported totals are rounded milestones, not a complete annual series.
sources.second_check: Headline totals, growth rate, regional contributions, and sector shares were checked in separate subsections of the same official report; long-run scenario context is supplied separately by NGFS.

sources.title: Energy and AI: Energy demand from AI
locators: Data centre electricity consumption in the Base Case
United States and China growth discussion
sources.verified_scope: Global total data-center electricity, historical estimate, Base Case to 2035, and high-efficiency/lift-off sensitivities.
critical_notes: Global share is small relative to total demand but load is spatially concentrated.
The report's total facility boundary must not be compared as if identical to AEO's server-only row.
sources.second_check: 2024, 2030, and 2035 figures were checked in the chapter and official executive-summary framing; facility scope was checked against report definitions.

sources.title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
sources.verified_scope: U.S. total data-center facility electricity, including servers, storage, networking, and infrastructure, with 2028 range.
critical_notes: 2028 is a range, not a point forecast.
Major uncertainties include GPU shipments, operating practice, cooling technology, and efficiency.
The model is constrained by proprietary and limited public data.
sources.second_check: Landing-page metadata, DOI record, PDF executive summary, component definition, and methods limitations were independently checked within the publisher's repository.

sources.title: Global EV Outlook 2026: Outlook for electric mobility
locators: Electricity demand, paragraphs accompanying the chart Electricity demand by mode and scenario, 2025, 2030 and 2035
sources.verified_scope: Global road-EV electricity demand in 2025 and CPS, STEPS, and NZE scenario milestones for 2035.
critical_notes: The CPS and NZE values are stated as exceeding thresholds and are encoded as lower bounds.
EV electricity is a component of total electricity demand, not an additional system total.
sources.second_check: Narrative milestones were checked against the official CC BY 4.0 chart page and its scenario/mode notes. Ambiguously mapped chart rows were not ingested.

sources.title: World Energy Outlook 2025: Executive summary
sources.verified_scope: Scenario-level direction and driver list through 2035; detailed proprietary scenario tables are not redistributed.
critical_notes: CPS, STEPS, and NZE are conditional scenarios, not predictions.
sources.second_check: Driver statements were checked against IEA Electricity 2026 and the sector detail in IEA Energy and AI and Global EV Outlook 2026.

sources.title: Air conditioning use emerges as one of the key drivers of global electricity-demand growth
locators: Global cooling demand, installed-unit, and efficiency findings
sources.verified_scope: Structural cooling driver and 2050 sensitivity from the Future of Cooling assessment.
critical_notes: This is an older structural scenario, not a current 2026 forecast.
Efficiency can materially reduce load growth.
sources.second_check: The article's values were checked against the official IEA Future of Cooling report framing linked by the publisher.

sources.title: The Future of Heat Pumps: Executive summary
sources.verified_scope: Heat-pump electrification as a power-demand driver and final-energy efficiency mechanism.
critical_notes: Heat pumps increase electricity use but can reduce total final energy required per unit of heat.
sources.second_check: Demand and efficiency statements were checked in separate sections of the official executive summary.

sources.title: Electrification Futures Study: Scenarios of Electric Technology Adoption and Power Consumption for the United States
sources.verified_scope: U.S. 2016 reference electricity and 2050 sector consumption under Reference, Medium, and High electrification with three technology-advancement cases.
critical_notes: This is an older scenario stress test based on an AEO2017-era baseline, not a current forecast.
Behind-the-meter EV charging can be attributed to buildings rather than transportation.
sources.second_check: All normalized endpoints were independently transcribed and re-summed from Table 7.1; scenario interpretation was checked against the official NREL study page.

sources.publisher: Network for Greening the Financial System; hosted by International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis
sources.title: NGFS Long-term Scenarios Phase 5.1
sources.verified_scope: Narrow World final-electricity subset for three IAMs, seven scenarios, 15 aggregate/subsector variables, and five-year intervals through 2100.
critical_notes: Scenarios are not forecasts.
Models are not observations and should be shown as a spread.
Aggregate and subaggregate variables overlap and cannot all be stacked together.
The subset is intentionally narrow to comply with database redistribution limits.
sources.second_check: A sampled bulk response was checked against separate official run, model, node, unit, and variable metadata before the narrow subset was downloaded.

sources.title: En-ROADS Technical Reference: Energy Demand
sources.verified_scope: Architecture reference for a global stock-flow demand module, not permission or code for a bit-for-bit simulator copy.
critical_notes: En-ROADS is for scenario exploration and explicitly is not a forecast.
The dashboard implementation must remain a clean-room, attributed model unless a separate SDK license is obtained.
sources.second_check: Demand categories were cross-checked against the official En-ROADS model-structure, supply, market, and calibration chapters.

excluded_or_deferred.item: IEA EV chart mode-by-mode CSV rows
excluded_or_deferred.reason: The downloaded numeric rows were visible but their ordered scenario/year categories were not exposed reliably in the accessible page representation. Narrative totals are retained; row mapping is deferred rather than guessed.

excluded_or_deferred.item: AEO Case Descriptions standalone data-center numeric table
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Extracted table labels were ambiguous relative to the workbook and official narrative. The complete workbooks and narrative are the source of record for normalized values.
No single future is scientifically justified. The package provides an IEA near-term forecast and multi-model NGFS conditional scenarios, retaining model spread.
